ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha 2b8ccac18a70 (2026-05-13T12:00:40Z) included a migration (20260513_add_order_events_status_index.exs) that added a new index on the high-churn `order_events` table but simultaneously disabled autovacuum on that table (set `autovacuum_enabled=false` as a migration side-effect to avoid lock contention during index creation) and never re-enabled it. The `order_events` table receives thousands of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations per minute from the order-processor service. Without autovacuum running, dead tuples accumulated rapidly — within ~40 minutes of the deploy the table reached 84% bloat (15.3 GB dead out of 18.3 GB total), causing sequential scans to read 13x more pages than necessary, query latency to explode past 45 seconds, lock contention cascading into connection pool exhaustion (100/100 connections), and complete unavailability of the checkout and order-processor services.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately re-enable autovacuum on the bloated table: `ALTER TABLE order_events SET (autovacuum_enabled = true);` 2. Manually trigger a VACUUM to reclaim dead tuples (avoid VACUUM FULL during peak traffic as it takes an exclusive lock): `VACUUM ANALYZE order_events;` — if bloat is too severe for standard VACUUM to recover enough space, schedule `pg_repack -t order_events` which works without exclusive locks. 3. Kill long-running transactions blocking autovacuum: `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event_type='Lock' AND query ~ 'order_events' AND state='active' AND query_start < now() - interval '5 minutes';` 4. Restart order-processor pods to clear connection pool state once postgres latency normalises. 5. In the migration file `20260513_add_order_events_status_index.exs` in sha 2b8ccac18a70, add `ALTER TABLE order_events SET (autovacuum_enabled = true);` at the end of the migration and redeploy. 6. Long-term: lower `autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor` for order_events to 0.01 and increase autovacuum worker count.
